snippet.title: 12 Dangerous Scenes Cobra Kai Actors Had To Film
snippet.description:
With Cobra Kai season 5 now streaming on Netflix, we can’t help but wonder about all the dangerous stunts and fight choreography these actors and stunt doubles went through. The performers on this show, like Mary Mouser and Peyton List, are no strangers to on-set injuries. We also have the return of Sean Kanan, a Karate Kid III alumni. We’re actually so lucky to have him because he suffered a near-fatal injury on set in the 80s. After fainting in Las Vegas, he found out that he only had minutes to live if he didn’t get to the hospital on time. It seems like Cobra Kai has always been rooted in danger. We also get into a few moments during the prom after-party fight sequence. Did you know that in a lot of movies and TV shows they actually wet the concrete to make the sidewalks and streets appear bigger on screen? Though this might be visually appealing, it really doesn’t help when trying to do fight choreography in high heels. Due to this environmental struggle, Peyton List fell on top of Mary Mouser and caused a serious injury to her hand. There are also some moments where the stunt doubles have to be thrown through glass panels more than once. There was a medic on set supergluing cuts together and cleaning up injuries so they could be reset for another take. Make sure to stick around until the end, as we’ll be getting into all of this show’s cuts, bruises, and mishaps that’ll make you appreciate the performer’s hard work even more.

snippet.title: All Of The Harry Potter Professor's Bloopers
snippet.description:
Harry Potter is full of quirky characters just a stone's throw away from the main cast. While Harry, Ron and Hermione are all charming in their own way, today we thought we’d look at some underappreciated characters in the stories. The professors. The professors are all freaking amazing characters and the actors behind them are hilarious geniuses. Emma Thompson gave one of the most amazing improvised bits in all of improv history while Professor Umbridge was speaking. And Umbridge behind the scenes is played by one goofy Imelda Staunton who’s best buds with Maggie Smith. The two together are a charming pair. Maggie once threatened to whack a student with a scroll. Of course, she didn’t mean it but it was funny. Maggie’s Professor McGonagall taught Ron to dance and Rupert insisted nobody ever breathe a word of the situation. Once, he doodled a picture of Alan Rickman and Rickman’s response might surprise you since we’re all so used to serious Severus Snape. He was such a genuine and kind guy who loved to laugh, especially with Michael Gambon. Michael and Alan played the most amazing prank on Daniel Radcliffe once. And once, while Radcliffe was hanging out in the side-car of Hagrid’s motorcycle, Robbie Coltrane started goofing around and made everyone on set giggle. Coltrane also celebrated over the thousandth take of a scene and somebody has yet to tell him that’s not a good thing. Warwick Davis went crowd surfing but that wasn’t the original plan. Richard Harris might have mistaken one of the animatronics for a real animal and the other Dumbledore had a knack for making Radcliffe laugh. While Miriam Margolyes, aka Professor Sprout, traumatized him.

snippet.title: Pinocchio Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
You can stream the new, live-action Pinocchio movie starring Tom Hanks, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, and Cynthia Erivo on Disney Plus. Director Robert Zemeckis has helped bring to life legendary films like Back to the Future and Forrest Gump, so naturally, he would have his own unique way of getting things done. Tom Hanks definitely had his hands full while portraying the complex Geppetto. He really had to have his acting skills top-notch because most of the time he was doing the entire scene – that would have Pinocchio and other characters added in post – by himself. One of the key things that makes him such a talented actor was his ability to really believe he was looking at the character, when in fact, nobody was there. If it looked like he was looking through Pinocchio, for example, instead of at him, it would’ve made the whole scene fall apart. Another legendary performance brought into the mix was Joseph Gordon-Levitt voicing Pinocchio’s conscience, Jiminy Cricket. Robert Zemeckis really helped him hone in on the voice of Jiminy Cricket by utilizing the way Joseph reads to his kids at night. When it came to Cynthia Erivo performing the classic, “When You Wish Upon A Star,” Robert Zemeckis was completely blown away by her. He didn’t even need her to do more than one take! Every take she did was apparently absolutely stunning. Stream the live-action Pinocchio on Disney Plus and let us know what you think of it in the comments.

snippet.title: 15 Painful Costumes And Prosthetics In The Rings Of Power
snippet.description:
Everyone’s talking about the new Amazon Prime series, The Rings of Power. While this series is a prequel to J.R.R. Tolkein’s famous Lord of the Rings franchise, it seems that The Rings of Power is appealing to Lord of the Rings fans and middle earth newbies, alike. This series is said to be the highest budget television show in history, and when you see it, it’s really no surprise. It’s clear that lots of money, thought, and effort went into making an imagined place feel real and fantasy species look as realistic as the rest of us. But, when it comes to transforming humans into orcs and dwarves, it’s not all about the budget, supplies, and the masterminds behind the prosthetics and makeup. The actors, themselves, have a lot to do with how well their physical transformations into their characters  are achieved, and sometimes it is way, way more difficult than they make it look. While being cast in a Lord of the Rings series is a dream to some, getting into the makeup and costumes required to be a part of Tolkein’s universe can be a bit more like a nightmare. To ten pound pairs of shoes to facial hair puzzles to those crazy realistic elf ears that you surely have a few questions about, we have lots of inside scoop on what went into bringing these characters to life. And, if you’re wondering why they didn’t use CGI instead, the upside of sitting in the makeup chair for hours, or how the cast ended up with a wig named… Gloria? Well, we’ve got all those details, too.

snippet.title: Harry Potter: Behind the Scenes Of The Triwizard Tournament
snippet.description:
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire gave us some of the best scenes in the entire franchise. The Triwizard tournament was so captivating we couldn’t help but want to talk about it! The work that went into the creation of the dragons deserves a round of applause or a bow or something. And not just the dragons but the creation of the scene. Daniel Radcliffe did one super dangerous stunt over and over again. The Yule Ball was rife with teens absolutely petrified of dancing. Rupert Grint learning to dance with Maggie Smith is filled with laughs behind the scenes. It’s just so precious! Radcliffe and Emma Watson are two of the most klutzy actors in the franchise. Emma’s dress was a serious stresser for her and so there were some things she just refused to do in it which was downright ridiculous of her. Daniel had far less time to learn to dance thanks to being the lead and so he’s just tripping all over his and other people’s feet. The scenes in the lake, we hate to break it to you, weren’t actually filmed in a lake. But can you guess just how much is CGI? And a lot of time went into putting on his fishy makeup and designing the merpeople. The maze was our first ever introduction to Voldemort so you know we’l be covering just how they made Ralph Fiennes’ face look like it did. And just for fun, we’re going to watch every single time Robert Pattinson was Avada Kedavra’d.

snippet.title: Stranger Things Actors Who Were Injured While Filming
snippet.description:
The Stranger Things actors work so hard to bring this incredible TV show to life, which means they’ve had to bear quite a few on-set injuries. Honestly, Jamie Campbell Bower’s terrifying Vecna presence should be counted as an injury on its own. Millie Bobby Brown not only had to deal with a broken knee while on set, but there were plenty of times that she lost her voice while filming intense scenes with Dacre Montgomery in season three. Speaking of Dacre Montgomery, he’s a method actor, so he really dove deep into the character of Billy. So deep, that he endured some pretty wild injuries whilst filming. Naturally, Sadie Sink’s character, Max, is a skater, so she had to learn to skate. Anyone who has ever skateboarded knows you can’t learn how to be a skater without taking a few falls – or a lot. We can also talk a lot about Natalia Dyer and all the stunt work she did in her scene with the Mind Flayed Tom Holloway. There were even stunts she wanted to do that the production team would not even allow her to try – it was probably for the best, looking back on the scene. Joe Keery is used to being right in the middle of the action. Do you remember his fight sequence at the Russian Base? Yeah, he performed all of his own stunts that day. There were quite a few injuries sustained throughout these scenes – we’ll be getting into all of that and so much more.

snippet.description:
Top Gun: Maverick was done practically and not CGI, which no doubt you know by now. So naturally, the entire movie was dangerous. Well, we’re not covering the entire movie but just the parts that have fun little anecdotes to go with it. Like Miles Teller being poisoned. Tom Cruise had the best comeback, too. Or how about a roof literally being detached thanks to the speed of the F-18s. Or maybe some of those insane stunts! Like flying over the mountains. Teller hit his head. Actually, Teller was having a pretty terrible time between that head whack and the poisoning. He genuinely thought he was a goner for a moment when one stunt got a little too close to real danger for his liking. Monica Barbaro might have lied to the director about her swimming ability during her audition. That could have seriously hurt her, or her career. The swimming training went so much farther than she could have anticipated. Imagine swimming. Now imagine swimming in a parachute. Now imagine swimmig in a parachute with sharks. We’re kidding about that last part. You can imagine it if you want, though. Tom Cruise was doing something silly on his motorbike that could have seriously done him in. Oh, and did we mention the vomit? Yeah, there was a lot of vomit. Everybody vomited. Except Monica. She did handstands before getting on the plane to get her head used to the weird pressure a bit. Everybody needs to be a bit more like Monica.

snippet.title: 12 Painful Scenes To Film In Thor
snippet.description:
Chris Hemsworth has been bringing Thor to life for eleven years now – with eleven years, comes a fair amount of pain and injury. With Taika Waititi direction both Thor: Ragnarok and Thor: Love and Thunder, there was so much freshness brought to the world and the character, including the incredible Natalie Portman stepping in as Mighty Thor. Natalie Portman had to train for months before the shoot and continue her training during production. Luckily, she had Chris Hemsworth there to show her the ropes and her good friend Tessa Thompson as her training buddy. We’re talking about a lot of asparagus and a lot of protein shakes. Natalie did as many stunts as she was able to on the set of Love and Thunder and one of the things that complicated it for her was actually the weight and design of her costume. Natalie wasn’t the only one with costume complaints – Tessa Thompson really struggled with her cape as well. With the countless times she tripped over it, or with the wind machine blowing it in her face, she had to have multiple sets of costumes as well. Not only were there wardrobe malfunctions, but there was definitely a fair amount of serious injuries on the set of Thor. One in particular had Jaimie Alexander out of shooting for months! Luckily she was able to make a full recovery, but the fall she took was pretty nasty! We’ll be getting into all of that and more – so make sure to stick around until the very end of the video.

George R. R. Martin is back with a stunning prequel to the most popular tv show ever, Game of Thrones! House of the Dragon is bigger, shinier, and sharper than ever. Seriously!! House of the Dragon has gone digital. Well, sometimes. They switch between green screens and LED panels. Another Weirwood tree has made its debut in the series but this one isn’t looking so grouchy as the one we saw in GoT. We will also be checking out how they film humans flying on the backs of dragons! Sadly, there’s no actual flight involved but you probably knew that already…

snippet.title: LOTR: The Rings Of Power Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Another J.R.R. Tolkein story is set to hit screens. Well, the little screen. The  Rings of Power is finally here to… mixed reactions. And the show isn’t even out yet! Did you hear how many injuries, and how much sweat and tears went into this project? Like, the three stunt people who seriously hurt themselves in the process. Amazon had to pay out a ton of money on that front. Yeah, we don’t think we’re selling the show very well… But the thoughtfulness that went into the costumes and the technology of Númenor! Did you know those boats are actually sailable? It would be a tricky sail but it’s possible! The height of the hobbits may have been altered digitally but the feet are all prosthetics. And while we are on the topic of scale, did you hear the actors had to go through scale academy because the heights of characters in this show are so all over the place? And as far as VFX go, the production company was bragging about how few digital effects they used but they used almost ten thousand. The orcs were mostly practically done, at least unless you look at the ones in the background. The queen’s armor was Cynthia Addai-Robinson’s favorite part of everything because she expected to be dolled up in dresses. Security was intense on this show. Finger scanning was used and everything! This is also Netflix - sorry - Amazon’s most expensive show to date (partially due to them beating out Netflix’s huge bid). And actors Benjamin Walker and Robert Armayo have more in common than you might think. Can you guess what connects them?

For all you die-hard Stranger Things fans out there - you’ve watched the series grow each time a new season rolled out. But did you know how much work production put into this show? Well it was - to put it lightly - a lot of hard work. Everything from the sets to costumes - not one Demogorgan was left unburned.
In order to have a successful series - you have to have a strong start. So casting was the first thing on the minds of the Duffer Brothers - and picking those kids was no easy task. But we know they nailed that aspect - what about the production design? Well, that concept only got bigger for them - as they proved to Netflix time and time again that they can deliver regardless of the budget. You know that everytime Millie Bobby Brown fought an upside down creature - that she worked completely with CGI? That’s a very difficult task to complete as a teen actor. And for Sadie Sink to flawlessly execute her almost demise in Season Four - is something out of a comic book! But sometimes production's creative alternatives - become classic visuals for the audience in the end.
So who’s ready to see Jamie Campbell Bower get put through the wringer for his Vecna design? We are! But seriously though - can we appreciate the time and effort these artists sacrificed to make one costume? And that one’s just a small slice on the pie - there’s literally copies of copies of everyone's costume on set. Some with the strangest of details!

snippet.title: Behind The Set Of Harry Potter And The Philosopher's Stone
snippet.description:
Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone was Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Rupert Grint’s first major role that shaped so many childhoods around the world. In this video, we’ll be talking about the magic behind the set. Did you know they used a ton of actual locations from places like England and Scotland? They used a combination of real-life, historic locations, practical set building, CGI, and animation to bring this film to life. J.K. Rowling had a vision for what she wanted Hogwarts to look like, so the crew traveled all over England to find churches and historic buildings to match it. Luckily for them, there are tons of buildings like that in England, so they didn’t have a hard time finding them. There was also a real, practical model of the Hogwarts Castle built by a team of eighty-six artists and crew members. It was used for a variety of different shots and blended together with CGI. One of the major locations – particularly Platform 9 ¾, was shot at King’s Cross Station. This train station holds a lot of significance for J.K. Rowling because that’s where her parents met for the first time. It makes sense that this would be the start of Harry Potter’s magical journey. That is one of the many train stations utilized in the making of this iconic film. Truly, the art department of this film could be considered wizards themselves because of how many incredible set pieces they made. Is anyone up for a game of ten-foot-tall chess? Stick around so we can expose all of Hogwarts’ behind the scenes’ secrets.

snippet.title: Marvel Actor Auditions And How They Landed The Role
snippet.description:
#mcu #marvel #tomholland 
The MCU is one of the most well known franchises in the world, and the actors within it are household names. From Tom Holland as Spider-Man, to Chris Evans as Captain America, it’s hard to imagine anyone else playing these iconic roles. But at one point, all of these positions were open for the taking, and things could have gone very differently. Some of your favorite actors almost didn’t land the roles you know them for. Even Black Widow was originally cast as someone else before Scarlett Johansson stepped in. The audition stories these actors have will give you a whole new perspective on what it takes to be cast in the MCU. From multiple rejections, to long-shot odds, this is how our favorite actors became our favorite heroes. 

Did you know multiple actors went for the role of Captain America, but ended up getting a different part in the MCU? There were a lot of close calls throughout the years that could have drastically changed the face of Marvel. Even Robert Downey Jr. wasn’t a sure thing at the time. There was a lot of doubt surrounding his casting. Could you imagine an MCU where Downey isn’t playing Iron Man? 

There is a boatload of talent laced throughout the MCU, and all the actors portraying our favorite heroes earned their parts with their impressive auditions. We love how everything shook out, and wouldn’t have it any other way!

Which audition did you find most interesting? Let us know in the comments!

snippet.title: 15 Painful Scenes The Spider Man Cast Had To Film
snippet.description:
Being Spider-Man is far from easy - and making the films is no different! From the silly to the downright dangerous, there isn’t much this team didn’t experience while making all the films. From Spider-Man: No Way Home, all the way back to the OG Spider-Man starring Tobey Maguire. 
The Green Goblin always makes for tricky filming - whether Willem Dafoe was sporting the old, clunky suit or the sleek new, upgraded one when he joined the No Way Home film. This crew was very good at making iconic shots look good - but they weren’t so great at doing it super easily! The cast struggled through filming solid landings, as well as nailing fights.
Oh, we have to mention the issue of water on set. On more than a couple occasions, Spider-Men have found themself quite literally drowning on set which has made their struggles through filming that much more epic! 
Now, Tom did have a ton of safety measures in place like harnesses, but just because he was able to film fairly safely didn’t make it less dangerous and tricky. Somehow, the actor managed to pull off wicked stunts despite discomfort. Emma Stone learned a thing or two about that when she was filming some stunts for The Amazing Spider-Man 2. Unfortunately, her safety equipment just made the job harder! Don’t even get us started on Tobey Maguire’s running into a literal burning building stunt - did anyone think of the ease of shooting at all?
The Spidey crew always brings it, thank goodness they made it through these difficult scenes mostly unscathed!

snippet.title: 15 Stranger Things Scenes That Made The Cast Cry For Real
snippet.description:
Where do we even begin with Stranger Things Season Four? The series as a whole has taken us on an emotional roller coaster - that made us cry A LOT. But did you know that this talented cast cried with us too? That’s right - even the emotionless Vecna let the tears flow a few times.
When working on a series for a period of time - you start to grow close with the cast and crew. As Jamie Campbell Bower’s time ended on set - he may or may not have cried in front of everyone in his Vecna prosthetics. It’s not just the departures that get to these actors however - it can sometimes just be the intense emotions played out in a scene. Both Millie Bobby Brown and Sadie Sink can attest to letting their real emotions get the best of them. But these moments of sincere crying are what really made those powerful moments - even stronger for the audience watching. It’s tough to think that Joe Keery had to go through heart breaks over and over again - but we’re sure he’s doing just fine after Season Four’s finale.
All an actor needs is a good script and direction - and luckily for the cast of Stranger Things - they get both! But while all good things come with a price - real emotions will start to come through. So let’s take a look at some of the times the cast cried for real on set - but sometimes not for the reasons you were thinking.

snippet.title: Ms. Marvel Scenes Without Special Effects
snippet.description:
Marvel VFX is no joke! Especially when it comes to this new and improved Disney Plus version of Ms. Marvel. When creating the iconic Kamala Khan, the creative time behind the show actually had to develop her powers from scratch – that’s a totally new thing in the MCU universe. They ended up playing around with color schemes and landing on blue as an ode to her hero, Captain Marvel, and eventually, Kamala Khan’s Hard Light powers were born. There are so many incredible visual effects in this vibrant miniseries. We’ve got small things like extras being placed in empty corners, to massive things like major explosions or elephant toothpaste spilling throughout the high school hallway. Did you know the VFX team spent more time on a twelve-second shot than anything else in the entire series? They also utilized set extensions for many places in the show including Jersey City itself, while still using actual references for their digital designs. When it came to the fight sequences, all of the weapons were created using VFX, which took several steps to complete – even Kamala’s ability to embiggen proved to be quite the challenge for this seasoned VFX team. One thing they did do practically, though, was utilize on-camera lighting to help bring Kamala’s telekinetic powers to life. They did quite the dance when it came to getting all those lightbulbs just right— they didn’t want to rely solely on the VFX team for it. Stick around until the end of the video to learn all the MCU’s VFX secrets.

snippet.title: The Voices Behind The Cuphead Show
snippet.description:
The Cuphead Show has an incredible cast behind the voices, like Tru Valentino as Cuphead, Frank Todaro as Mugman, Joe Hanna as Elder Kettle, Wayne Brady as King Dice, and Luke Millington-Drake as the Devil. When it came to Tru Valentino's Cuphead voice, we've got his East Coast mother and some old-school mobster movies to thank for it. The creators always knew they wanted Cuphead and Mugman to sound like they were from the East Coast, but Tru Valentino and Frank Todaro took the voices to a whole new level comedically. Frank Todaro describes it as a collaborative process -- he's just a cog in the Cuphead wheel, as he describes it. We’ve also got the incredible addition of the hilarious Natasia Demetriou, who you might recognize as Nadja from What We Do in the Shadows. She was brought on as Cala Maria — yes that is a play on the dish, calamari. In the Cuphead video game, Cala Maria is a big boss who is no joke to fight — in the show, she is equally as scary and quite hilarious with the talented Natasia behind her. If you’ve seen her in What We Do in the Shadows, you would understand why we are so excited to see her performance as the sassy sea monster. We also can't forget that talented Grey DeLisle who has voiced an insane amount of characters from shows like Dexter's Labratory, Rugrats, Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends, Scooby-Doo and many, many more.

snippet.title: 15 Painful Scenes To Film In Prey
snippet.description:
In the Predator franchise’s newest movie, Prey, Amber Midthunder plays Naru, Predator’s first major foe. In this action film directed by Dan Trachtenburg, there were a ton of major stunt sequences to pull off and a lot of challenges that came with them. One thing we’re going to talk a lot about is Dane Diliegro’s practical Predator suit. Wearing it was one of the major challenges that came attached to this film. While he was inside of it, he couldn’t really see or hear anything. They had to help him get through the fight sequences with earpieces and sticks on the ground. There was also a major malfunction after one of his scenes that could have been extremely dangerous. Not only that, but the mud pit – which was nothing like a day at the spa – apparently smelled so foul that the cast could hardly stand to be around it. The irony of that is it only started to smell after they’d been inside of it. Cleaning off all of that mud was also a huge inconvenience – when it came to that mud, no one was able to catch a break. Dakota Beavers, who plays Taabe, also had a few difficult experiences when trying to perform his stunts. He wanted to do as many as he was allowed to – so bad, in fact, that he wouldn’t speak up about the injuries he received because he didn’t want them to take him off. Make sure you stick around because we’ll be getting into all of that and every other painful mishap that took place on this set.

snippet.title: Stranger Things Cast React To Season 4 Scenes
snippet.description:
The Stranger Things cast are all huge fans of the show and are stunned time and again by the Duffer Brothers’ ability to keep things fresh and really honour the eighties vibes, even into season 4. The scene in Vecna’s mind layer had Gaten on the edge of his seat, and Sadie stunned at the VFX. The guitar shredding solo had Joseph Quinn gutted that he was leaving the show but so thrilled that he got to fulfill a childhood fantasy, at least for a day. Max’s sacrifice was giving the cast chills. We wonder how Sadie felt about watching her bones snap on screen. Editing is everything when it comes to this show. That’s what shook Caleb the most was the way the stories were intertwined. Finn Wolfhard’s a pro and only needed a few shots at his monologue. It blew Charlie Heaton’s mind and Eduardo Franco was kind of… out of his mind. Steve was thrilled he finally got to use those swimming skills he learned for season 1. Joseph Quinn was feeling a bit weird about taking over as side-Joe in season 4 to be Dustin’s new partner in proving-his innocence. But some goofy things Gaten did kept things interesting and light and even created a friendship between the two Joes. The debate over whether Steve should shave is definitely one of the highlights of season 4. Natlie felt a little guilty for her character’s inability to make the best morally right decisions. Noah was thrilled to get out of Hawkins. Charlie Heaton loved his role in the long-distance love triangle. Eduardo Franco found parallels between his entrance to the show and his character’s experience. Yes, the cast is passionate about Stranger Things season 4.

snippet.title: Day Shift Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
The Netflix movie Day Shift has an all-star cast with Jamie Foxx, Dave Franco, Snoop Dogg, and Karla Souza behind it, but they also have an incredible crew to back them up. J.J. Perry is no stranger when it comes to directing amazing action movies. In this horror-comedy, Jamie Foxx plays a struggling father who uses a pool cleaning job as a cover for his real one – hunting vampires. Something that gives this movie a fresh take on an age-old concept definitely has something to do with the incredible stunts and action sequences behind it. J.J. Perry, who also worked as the stunt coordinator in John Wick, wanted real contortionists to recreate the vampire’s movements. He also choreographs an amazing, and practical, car chase sequence with an RPV drone technique we’ve never seen before. He claims that by his next movie, he’s going to have reinvented car chases. Jamie Foxx also has some hilarious moments while working on the set of this film. Did you know that he’s kind of a musical genius? First-day jitters are unheard of when Jamie Foxx is producing professional songs based on a cool line that you said on camera. Though they did have a lot of fun on set, one thing Karla Souza was not too happy with were her vampire fangs – they made it way more difficult for her to work, and they were also pretty painful at times. Stick around until the end, ‘cause we’ll be biting into all of that and so much more.

snippet.title: The Voices Behind Arcane Characters
snippet.description:
Arcane is one of the best adaptations of a video game we’ve ever seen. Part of that success came from the fantastic group of actors that were hired on. They all come from such different backgrounds, too. Hailee Steinfeld, known for Hawkeye and her amazing singing voice combed through Reddit forums to learn more about her character Vi. She and Ella never once worked together. Ella Purnell, who voiced Jinx had never done voice acting before and put on an accent for the role and also refused to look at anything online. Katie Leung, probably best known for her portrayal of Cho Chang in the Harry Potter Series also had to do an accent. The hype of the IP stopped her from looking online too much. Mia Sinclaire Jenness who played the young Powder gave a performance that brought people to tears. Mick Wingert’s dynamic performance is what landed him the role of Heimerdinger because they were super hesitant to even include the character in the show. Kevin Alejandro, known for his role in Lucifer, took the role of Jayce seriously thanks to his thirteen year old son. Harry Lloyd, known for playing Daenerys Targaryen’s cruel brother in Game of Thrones, loved the reverse process he got to do for his character Viktor. JB BLanc came straight from the League of Legends video game as he voiced Braum but for the show he voiced Vander. Silco doesn’t exist in the video game so Jason Spisak enjoyed the mysterious element to his character. Creators Alex Yee and Christian Linke not only encouraged improv but also wanted the actors to add their own special touch to their characters. And of course, Imagine Dragons and J.I.D. blew our minds with that song Enemy. All that and more in the video!

snippet.title: These Prey scenes were almost impossible to film… #shorts
snippet.description:
#shorts #predator #prey 
The Predator franchise just keeps pushing the bar of visual effects. But do you know what it’s like being the Predator in the new Prey Movie? Not so fun - according to Dane DiLiegro.

snippet.title: Prey Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
Is Prey perhaps the best Predator movie yet? With incredible prosthetics, relying only on CGI when absolutely necessary, it’s leaving Dane DiLiegro with such a pain in the neck. Or maybe not, he did some special neck training to prep for staring at the ground with a giant murderous helmet on. He wasn’t the only one prepping. The cast had to go through bootcamp. Four weeks of it. Dakota Beavers had to learn to ride a horse. Amber Midthunder had to learn to use weapons. All sorts of weapons. When designing a vision, sometimes it can be hard to decide what stays and what is left on the cutting room floor. When you’re working with a prequel, it’s important your villains aren’t half-baked but also aren’t overwhelmingly powerful. They need somewhere to go, right? So deciding what powers the Predator kept and lost was a challenge. The cute dog Coco didn’t have many aspirations before Prey but now she’s living in the lap of luxury. There was plenty in Prey to not enjoy filming from shooting with smoke to the mud pit. The mud pit was absolutely nasty so said, Amber. Was it even mud? We have our suspicions. Not every scene makes it into a movie. In Prey, that scene was a chase from the trees. How sad. The director wanted all of his fights to be vertical though. Designers, man, they’re so picky! Valiantly leaping from the backs of horses and braving treacherous rivers sounds like a pretty intense shoot to us!

snippet.title: The Making Of House Of The Dragon
snippet.description:
We couldn’t be more excited to talk about the new Game of Thrones spinoff, House of the Dragon. We get to learn the entire history and backstory of the infamous Targaryen house. With George R. R. Martin’s incredible writing, backed up by the dedicated cast and crew, we’re definitely in for a ride. In this video, we’ll be talking about everything from how the dragons were shot, to the unfortunate on-set injuries that this powerhouse of a cast pushed through. There are so many incredible locations the show was shot in, it makes sense that they would have magnificent set-pieces to match – we’re looking at you, King’s Landing. Not only do we have the pleasure of exploring unique and stunning locations in England, but they also take a trip to European countries like Spain and Portugal to capture quite a few moments. One thing George R. R. Martin shares with us was that this story was inspired by actual history. House of the Dragon was inspired by a generational, familial war after the fall of Henry I. We get to see a ton of actual, historical references peppered throughout the season. We’re not totally sure, but we think all the wigs fall under iconic historical moments. You’d be surprised just how long these actors spend in the makeup chair because of them. Stick around until the end of the video to indulge in everything we could find on House of the Dragon.

snippet.title: Stranger Things Cast Crazy Audition Stories
snippet.description:
Now that Stranger things is such a huge success it might seem as though the cast was always meant to be. However, when the creators The Duffer Brothers started their journey of casting, some people fit like a glove and others took many months of hemming and hawing over the perfect fit. This video will deep dive into how wild the casting process was, and how many thanks should be owed to casting director extraordinaire Carmen Cuba. This video has all the crazy tales of who was sick for their audition. Who didn’t even have to audition? Who said they could rollerskate professionally when the truth was a little to the left of that answer? Who’s son had to convince them to do the show in the first place? Who had their role tailor-made to fit their personality? Which audition was the funniest? Who was a broadway caliber performer? Who spoke in an American answer the entire audition process, including when they were out of character. Which actor “called” to the casting director”? And which actor needed the big break of Stranger Things to show the star he always was? Who thought they bombed their audition, and then after receving a callback, thought they bombed their callback? Who auditioned with an excerpt from the script of Hellraiser? And who danced in a G-String to seal the deal of their character? 
Discover the answers to all this and more. With all these crazy stories, it’s a miracle the cast of Stranger Things' chemistry is off the charts perfect. And for all you Stranger Things needs, be sure to like and subscribe to The Things!

snippet.title: Behind the Set Of Thor Love and Thunder
snippet.description:
Thor: Love And Thunder is electrifying and a big part of that is thanks to the sets and CGI.It’s brighter, it’s bigger, it’s more colorful, and it’s all thanks to the innovative minds that got together and created some awesome new tech. Like, the cool lighting system that can capture six different lightings of actors in one shot. And guess what? This isn’t a post-production thing, this is happening in real-time! Don’t believe us? You’re just going to have to watch to understand. Although, they can also do that stuff in post-production and do. Did you know Marvel movies basically plot out the entire movie in pre-vis and it’s like a little animated movie you’ll never get to see? New Asgard is one of the biggest sets most of these Marvel actors have ever been on. At least, that’s the case for Chris Hemsworth. And well, for one scene in the movie, they had to get some additional photography. So they had to completely remake the set digitally. How they did it is answered in the video. Remember when surround sound became a thing? Probably not. Well, surround environments are the new thing using LED panels literally all over the place. To the left. To the right. Up above. Just not in front of the camera. It’s game-changing. Despite all of this amazing tech, the movie has been criticised for poor CGI work and Taika Waititi has something to say about that… Well, really he doesn’t. He doesn’t care too much. The movie’s still a lot of fun. Don’t you agree?

snippet.title: Behind The Scenes Of The Sandman
snippet.description:
Neil Gaiman’s “The Sandman” is one of DC comics’ most incredible, record-breaking pieces of work. It makes sense that it would become one of TV’s most highly-anticipated shows. In this video we’ll be talking about everything that went into making such a complex, enthralling work of art. From Tom Sturridge’s intense character transformation, being locked in a glass sphere, totally naked for hours on end, to the incredible practical effects, Matthew, the iconic talking raven, from John Constantine becoming Johanna Constantine, to Neil Gaiman sharing his original scripts with the VFX supervisor, we’ve really got a lot to unpack. Did you know that they actually have a real, live raven on set to help encapsulate all that is Matthew? And that the voice of the characters is so spot on because the writer, Allan Heinberg wrote every single one with the actor’s voice in mind. There were also so many different costume iterations for all the characters. Tom Sturridge wanted to look as close to the comic book character as possible, but after bringing that look to life, it actually ended up looking more comedic than anything else, so they decided to go with a more natural look. We’ll be getting into all that and more, so stick around as we take you through Dream’s beautifully complicated timeline.
